title: Nanopore Sequencing of Poliovirus Isolates: Analysis and Quality Control
author: Ben Bellekom
materials: Run the PIRANHA analytical software once the sequencing run is complete. For full details on PiranhaGUI installation and usage visit https://github.com/polio-nanopore/piranhaGUI .
Open PiranhaGUI (click “Install update to PIRANHA software” if piranha needs to be updated)

steps.title: Perform Post-Sequencing Run Checks
steps.instruction: Manually verify the sequencing run success using the MinKNOW run report based on two criteria.

substeps.instruction: Confirm the sequencing run completed its full duration.
Confirm there was no sudden reduction in pore numbers (pores must not fall below 400 or 25% of total pores in the first hour).

steps.title: Troubleshoot Failed Sequencing Runs
steps.instruction: If the post-sequencing checks fail, perform the following based on the failure reason:

substeps.instruction: If the run did not reach full duration: Check MinKNOW system messages for alerts and restart the run. Ensure >500 pores are available; if not, repeat library pooling, library preparation, and load into a new flow cell.
If there was a sudden reduction in pore numbers in the first hour: If the run fails QC after Piranha analysis, repeat sample pooling, library preparation, and load into a new flow cell.

steps.title: Initialize PiranhaGUI Analysis
steps.instruction: Launch the PiranhaGUI software and configure the data paths.

substeps.instruction: Open Docker (update to latest if prompted).
In the setup window, select the 'Samples' field to provide the location of the barcode.csv file.
Select the 'MinKnow Run' field to provide the location of the demultiplexed fastq files (usually the fastq_pass folder).
Select the 'Output Folder' to specify where report files will be saved.
Click 'Continue' to enter the run window and select the maximum number of threads for the pipeline.

steps.title: Configure Piranha Analysis Options
steps.instruction: Set the specific analysis parameters for isolates.

substeps.instruction: Click 'Piranha Options' and set: Minimum read length: 1000, Maximum read length: 1300, Minimum depth: 50, and Minimum read percentage: 0.

steps.title: Set Persistent Run Options
steps.instruction: Configure the phylogenetic module and sample metadata in the 'Persistent Run Options' menu.

substeps.instruction: Under 'Supplementary directory for phylogenetic module', select the laboratory sequence database containing vp1_isolate_sequences.fasta files.
Under 'Orientation', select the barcode primer plate orientation (Horizontal or Vertical).
Under 'Protocol', select the sample type as 'stool'.
Enter or change names of positive and negative controls (separate multiple controls with commas).
Click 'Continue' to confirm changes.

steps.title: Execute and Verify Piranha Analysis
steps.instruction: Run the analysis and confirm successful completion.

substeps.instruction: Click 'Start Analysis' and monitor the progress bar.
Verify success by checking that the last line before '###PIRANHA SOFTWARE FINISHED###' is 'Generating: /data/run_data/output/piranha_output/report.html'. Resolve any errors if this line is missing.

steps.title: Perform Run Quality Control (RunQC)
steps.instruction: Evaluate the run success using the Piranha interactive HTML report and the detailed_run_report.

substeps.instruction: Verify if the positive control yielded >50 reads mapped to Coxsackievirus A20.
Verify if the negative control yielded <50 reads mapped to poliovirus or NPEVs.
Verify if the positive control had <50 reads that were NOT Coxsackievirus A20.
If all are 'Yes', enter 'Pass' in the 'RunQC' column of the detailed_run_report.

If any are 'No', enter 'Fail' in 'RunQC', add an explanation in 'comments', and troubleshoot: 
- Too few positive reads: Confirm positive control QC, repeat library pooling, verify library via Tapestation/Qubit, check adaptor (LA) and short fragment buffer (SFB), and check enzyme expiration dates.
- Too many negative reads: Confirm negative control QC, rewash flow cell with DNAse wash, and repeat library pooling and sequencing.
- Extra detection in positive control (>50 reads non-Coxsackievirus A20): Perform deep clean of workstations/pipettes with nucleic acid degradation solution (e.g., DNA Away, DNAZap) and retest samples.

steps.title: Generate Phylogenetic Tree
steps.instruction: Compare the current run to previous data using one of two methods.

substeps.instruction: Method A: Open the Piranha HTML report and confirm the presence of the phylogenetic tree and the identical sequences table.
Method B: Use Geneious or Nextstrain to align and generate a tree using the Piranha sequences and the laboratory sequence QC database.

steps.title: Perform Individual Sample QC
steps.instruction: Assess each sample and mark 'Pass' or 'Fail' in the 'SampleQC' column of the detailed_run_report.

substeps.instruction: Mark as 'Fail' if a pair of samples with the same EPID differ by 3 or more nucleotides over VP1.
Mark as 'Fail' if a sample is identical to another sample with a different EPID (unless both are the same Sabin serotype with ≤1 mutation from the original vaccine).

Check for bleed-through/contamination: Mark as 'Fail' if a sample matches a sequence from a previous run (with the same barcode) by <3 nucleotides over VP1, or if identical sequences appear at low read numbers across multiple samples.

steps.title: Perform Isolate Classification QC
steps.instruction: For samples that passed initial SampleQC and are programmatically relevant, perform case-level (EPID) classification.

substeps.instruction: For each sample within an EPID, mark 'Pass' if there are >500 reads mapping to the detected virus.
Mark 'Retest' if there are <500 reads but the consensus is classified as WPV or VDPV, or if <500 reads map to a virus expected by ITD.
If <500 reads and classified as NPEV or Sabin-like (and not expected by ITD), do not report and do not perform further testing.
Ensure all expected ITD classifications are detected and meet read criteria across all associated samples for an EPID to pass.

steps.title: Manage Retesting Process
steps.instruction: Process samples marked for retesting in a new sequencing run.

substeps.instruction: Repeat retested samples in a new run using the Y7/Q8 primer set, using different barcodes than the original run and not grouping them together.
Flag 'IsclassificationQCRetest' as 'Yes' in the new run.

Evaluate retest results: 
- Same sequence as initial run: Mark 'Pass'.
- Same sequences as first run but differ by ≥3 nucleotides (same EPID): Mark 'Pass'.
- Virus detected as expected by ITD after initial negative: Mark 'Pass'.
- No longer yield sequences: Mark as negative under 'IsolateClassification' and add 'Likely contamination' to 'QCComments' in the original run; remove from further analysis.
If samples remain negative despite expected ITD result, refer to GSL guidance.

steps.title: Finalize Reporting and Documentation
steps.instruction: Complete the final reports and archive the data.

substeps.instruction: For samples passing SampleQC: Mark 'SampleQCCheckComplete' as 'Yes' and 'ToReport' as 'Yes' (or 'Yes&Retest' if reporting immediately while a retest is pending).
For samples marked 'Retest': Mark 'SampleQC' as 'Retest', 'ToReport' as 'No', and add explanation to 'QCComments'.
Add EPIDs and metadata to the detailed_run_report.csv.
Once submitted, complete the 'DateReported' column.
Compile required reporting files: MinKNOW Run Report, Piranha output report, barcode_reports, QC detailed run report (including anomalies/corrective actions), and Fasta files of positive samples.

Update the laboratory sequence QC database: Append the run name to 'vp1_isolate_sequences.fasta' (e.g., 'vp1_isolate_sequences_run21.fasta'), append 'QC_Pass' to sequences that passed Run and Sample QC, and transfer the file to the database folder.
After retesting is complete, mark 'SampleQCChecksComplete' as 'Yes' in the original run.

description: report: This contains the sample summary information specific to the sequences generated for each sample.
